criteria.criterion: The design has an Existing code section that reuses or extends crates/athena-core/src/routing.rs and docs/design/ci-routing.md, describing how checks get results today: CI result requested first, polled up to ci_wait_s, local checks only as fallback.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. Section 1 cites routing.rs lines 10 to 20, which match the module comment I read: every kind but build asks ci_result::resolve, the GitHub push run is read every CI_POLL up to the bound, and NoCi applies with no GitHub origin or in a nested run. It also cites athena.toml line 46 ci_wait_s = 1500 (checked by Grep), local checks as the fallback, and ci-routing.md section 4.1's target cache key.

criteria.criterion: The Problem section gives measured durations for the CI-reuse path and the local-run path from recorded jobs (ci_result source and duration) or THROUGHPUT.md, with the source of each number and any unmeasured number labeled an estimate, and states what share of jobs run checks locally.
criteria.evidence: The note gives one CI-run figure (463 s, from an October job) and one local sample (job 20261101-061448-sdya: 2.4 s / 34.6 s / 1119.4 s, which matches its verification.json). It labels the CI wait an estimate of 8 to 15 minutes. That number could have been measured: 52 November brief-verifier.md files in the evidence each record a CI run duration, from 400 s to 690 s (most 450 to 650 s). The local path has 8 records, but only one was used. The note also states that the 14.1-minute median 'is dominated by the CI-wait path'. Records contradict this: only 3 of the 434 October verification records dated before the review reuse CI, so the review window ran almost entirely locally. The 52-of-61 count does not match the snapshot either: 58 November verification.json files, 50 with reused:true.

criteria.criterion: The 'Why this removes the bottleneck' section is derived from those per-path numbers, scales the 8.0-minute predicted saving to the local-fallback share, and says plainly if most jobs would not benefit, with a recommendation.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. The derivation is there, but its inputs and recommendation have the errors listed in the findings.

findings.summary: The claim that the 14.1-minute median is mostly CI wait is false, and records that would have shown this were readable.
findings.evidence: Review 20261029-155931-wfkr covers 279 landings up to 2026-10-29. Among the 434 October verification.json files in the evidence snapshot, only 16 have reused:true, and only 3 of those are dated before the review (Oct 10 twice, Oct 16), plus Oct 27. The window ran checks locally for almost every job. The bounded push-run polling was added later, by job 20261101-061448-sdya on 2026-11-01. The note's '15 percent is a lower bound for older months' hides this. A better approach: report the October local share from the records, and state that the CI-reuse change, not a warm baseline, has already moved the stage away from 14.1. The next review's comparison against 14.1 depends on that.

findings.summary: The CI-path duration is a guess (8 to 15 minutes) and one October sample, although 52 measured CI run durations were in the records.
findings.evidence: Grep 'CI run \S+ \(\d+s\)' over records/jobs/2026-11 matches 52 brief-verifier.md files, with durations from 400 s to 690 s. The local path likewise has 8 records, but only one was used. The default 'evidence' rule says a number that could be measured should be measured. A median of the recorded durations per path would have been simple and correct.

findings.summary: The headline recommendation is to restore the target cache on pull-request branches and split test across jobs, but the CI workflow already does both.
findings.evidence: ci-routing.md line 128: 'Pull-request runs restore it and do not save it.' The target-cache restore steps in .github/workflows/ci.yml (e.g. lines 157-161, 260-264, 369-373) have no event condition, so they run on every event, including push runs on athena/ci/**. The test job uses a shard strategy (ci.yml line 344, 'test shard 0'). The note says restore on pull-request runs is something 'section 4.1 currently does not do'. That misreads the document the note cites, so the recommended next step is work already built.

summary: This change fails. Only the design note and its CHANGELOG entry change, as scoped. The note describes the current CI-first flow correctly against routing.rs and athena.toml. It corrects the mtime freshness claim, scales the 8.0-minute prediction by the local share (0.6 minutes, labeled an estimate), says plainly that most jobs would not benefit, and keeps the review citation and the measurement plan. But checking its numbers and recommendation against the evidence snapshot turned up three major problems. First, the note says the review's 14.1-minute median is mostly CI wait. In fact almost every job in that window ran checks locally: only 3 of the 434 October verification records dated before the review reused CI. Second, it estimates the CI-path time at 8 to 15 minutes, although 52 recorded CI run durations (400 to 690 s) were readable. Third, its main recommendation is to restore the target cache on pull-request runs and split test across jobs, but ci-routing.md and ci.yml show both are already done. Criterion 2 is unmet, and the other two problems are major soundness findings. I checked all of this by reading the diff, the cited files and the evidence snapshot; I ran no build or test commands.
